story: Isis was sister and wife to Osiris, both children of the earth god Geb and the sky goddess Nut, part of a divine family descended from a creator god. When the creator passed down rule through the male line, Osiris became king and Isis his queen. Their brother Set killed Osiris and dismembered his corpse. Isis and her sister Nephthys, aided by another deity, searched for the scattered pieces and reassembled them. Isis's grief, sexual desire, and magical spells stirred Osiris back to life; she restored his breath, copulated with him, and conceived their son Horus, though afterward Osiris could live only in the underworld. Isis gave birth to Horus in the papyrus thickets of a river delta after a long, difficult labor, then had to protect the infant from Set and from snakes, scorpions, and illness. Seven minor scorpion deities guarded her; when a wealthy woman refused Isis shelter, the scorpions stung the woman's son, and Isis healed the innocent child out of compassion. Isis and Horus were sometimes shown in conflict: once Horus beheaded her, and she replaced her head with that of a cow. As Horus grew, he challenged Set for the kingship, and Isis helped him by using cunning and magic—once transforming into a young woman to trick Set into condemning his own usurpation of the throne, and later using her powers of transformation to destroy Set and his followers. In another tale, Isis served as a midwife alongside other goddesses at the birth of three future kings, calling out their names as each was born.
